title: text: the CJK system-font search no longer keeps every probed font file in memory (#769)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #769.

`cjk::system_font()` checked each non-italic system face with `Face::has_char`, which goes through `Face::bytes` and keeps the whole font file in the face's `OnceLock` for the life of the process. When the preferred families are not found (PingFang on macOS lives outside the scanned folders), every system face was read and kept: about 3.2 GB on the reporter's Mac.

- New `Face::covers_text(&str)`: if the face's file is not loaded yet, it reads the file into a temporary buffer, checks the charmap and drops the buffer. Faces that are already loaded (bundled, shared, or cached) use `has_char` as before.
- `cjk::system_font()` uses it, so only the chosen face's bytes stay in memory (copied once into egui's `FontData`, as before).
- `i18n::system_japanese_font()` has the same search loop (run when the interface is switched to Japanese without craft-fonts), so it uses `covers_text` too. Its doc comment already says only the chosen face's file is read; now that is true.

Face selection is unchanged: same samples, same preferred-family order, same weight tie-break.

Test: `fonts::tests::covers_text_does_not_keep_file_bytes` writes Inter to a temp file, builds a file-backed `Face`, checks `covers_text` gives the right answer (Latin + Cyrillic yes, Hebrew no), and that the face's byte cache is still empty afterwards. Loading through `data()` still fills it.

Not changed: sharing one buffer between the faces of a `.ttc`, deferring the search, and locating PingFang through Core Text. The issue lists these as alternatives; with this change only one face is kept, so they are not needed for the memory figure.

title: Timeline: draw each audio track's own waveform, not track 1's (#770)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #770.

**Cause:** timeline waveform peaks were computed with `MediaSource::audio`, which always reads audio stream 0, and cached per `ItemId` only. Every clip cut from a multi-stream file (e.g. an MKV with 4 audio tracks) therefore drew stream 0's waveform, whatever its `audio_stream` was, even though playback already uses the right stream.

**Fix:**
- The peak cache (`peaks`, `peaks_pending`, `peak_max`) is now keyed by `(ItemId, audio stream index)`.
- `draw_waveform` asks for the clip's own `it.audio_stream`; peaks are read with `MediaSource::audio_stream`, which the MKV and MP4 sources already implement (and which falls back to `audio` for stream 0 on single-stream sources).
- The peak loop moved into a small `source_peaks(src, stream, dur)` helper so it can be tested without a UI.
- Nested sequences (their mix) and the source monitor waveform keep using key/stream 0, as before.
- **Clip ▸ Generate Audio Waveform** (`clip.generateAudioWaveform`), which drops cached peaks so they are rebuilt, now drops every stream's entry for that item.

**Test:** `each_audio_stream_gets_its_own_waveform_peaks` uses a fake source whose stream 0 and stream 1 hold different constant levels, and checks that stream 1's peaks are its own and that a missing stream yields no peaks. With the old stream-0-only read it fails on the stream 1 assertion. Existing tests that read the peak cache (`nest_rendering_ui`, `scripted`) were updated for the new key.

body:
## What this does

H.265 export through NVENC was limited to Windows. This enables it on 64-bit Linux with NVIDIA's driver: Main 8-bit SDR and Main 10 HDR (PQ and HLG). It uses the CUDA device the H.264 NVENC encoder already uses on Linux, so there is no new FFI.

## Changes

- `nvenc/export.rs`: the HEVC factory is no longer Windows only.
- `lib.rs`: NVENC registration (format probe, HDR probe, warm HEVC probe, encoder factory) moved into one `register_nvenc()` used by Windows and Linux.
- On Linux it runs after the VA-API and NVDEC probes. Run beside the VA-API probe, the background HEVC probe's first `cuInit` can deadlock with libva-nvidia-driver, which calls `cuInit` from its library constructor under the loader lock. I hit this as a hang at 100% CPU in the export tests.
- The six `nvenc_hevc*.rs` tests and `nvenc_rgba_input.rs` now also build and run on Linux.
- Docs updated where they said H.265 NVENC export was Windows only.

## Testing

RTX 3080, driver 615.71.09, Linux, rebased on current main.

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`: pass.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 2,754 passed, 0 failed.
- All NVENC HEVC tests pass on the GPU (22 tests, including the real export job to MP4 and QuickTime and the HDR PQ and HLG exports checked with ffprobe).
- `nvenc_rgba_input.rs`: 3 passed on Linux.
- `filmcraft-cli --demo export out.mp4 --format hevc`: ffprobe reads hevc, Main, hvc1, yuv420p, 1920x1080, 72 frames. `ffmpeg -xerror` decodes it clean.

Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm target on my machine). Not tested on Windows, where the only change is the move into `register_nvenc()`.

title: #424: Render In to Out renders only the frames between In and Out
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G16 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #424.

## Problem
Sequence ▸ Render Effects In to Out (and Render In to Out) picked every render-bar segment that In/Out overlapped and rendered it in full. Segments run between edit points, so In/Out inside one long clip with effects rendered the whole clip, often the whole timeline.

## Fix
`crates/engine/src/previews.rs`
- The In/Out modes render only the marked frames of each segment. A segment that extends past In/Out gets a partial preview `<hash>-<off>-<len>.mov`, frames counted from the segment start, so a ripple that moves the segment keeps it, as it keeps whole `<hash>.mov` previews (still written when a render covers the whole segment; existing preview folders stay valid).
- The store indexes the parts per segment hash. The render bar is green over the rendered frames only, and a segment's `state` is green only when it is fully covered (`bar_json` adds `renderedFrames`). Playback reads the part holding the frame. Every mode renders only frames that have no preview yet, so a later render fills just the gaps.
- Delete Render Files In to Out deletes only the files that hold marked frames.
- File names read from disk are parsed defensively: u32 offsets, nonzero lengths, clamped to the segment, saturating math.

## Tests
New `previews_tests::render_in_to_out_renders_only_the_marked_frames`, on a Universal Counting Leader clip whose frames all differ. With In/Out at 6..11 inside a 24-frame segment it renders 6 frames (old code: 24, the test fails), and the bar is yellow/green/yellow. The preview of frame 9 matches the live frame 9. The parts survive re-indexing the folder. Rendering the whole sequence afterwards renders only the 2 gaps (18 frames) and the segment turns green. Delete In to Out over 7..8 removes only the middle part. The existing preview tests are unchanged and pass.

title: #647: decode E-AC-3 (Dolby Digital Plus) audio
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #647.

## Problem
Files with E-AC-3 (Dolby Digital Plus) audio imported with no sound. MP4 (`ec-3`), MOV, Matroska (`A_EAC3`) and MPEG-TS all detected the codec, but `filmcraft-ac3` refused bsid 11–16 with `Error::Unsupported`.

## Fix
- **`filmcraft-ac3`**: clean-room E-AC-3 decoding from ATSC A/52:2012 Annex E (new `eac3.rs`, spec sections listed in the crate README). It covers the full bsi (mixing and informational metadata are parsed and skipped) and the audfrm: 1/2/3/6 blocks per syncframe, reduced sample rates, per-block and frame-based exponent strategies (Table E2.10), syntax-enable flags with their defaults, SNR offset strategies 1–3, converter fields and block start info. Exponents can be reused across syncframes of fewer than six blocks; the decoder keeps them until `reset`. Spectral extension (§E3.6) is implemented: band structure, coordinates, blending, translation with wrap, the notch filter and noise blending. The audio blocks share the AC-3 path, and AC-3 output is unchanged (same SNR on every AC-3 oracle stream before and after).
- Independent substream 0 is decoded. Dependent substreams and other programs decode to no channels (`Header::is_primary`), so a 7.1 stream plays as its 5.1 core. The adaptive hybrid transform (only when a channel actually uses it) and enhanced coupling are refused with `Unsupported`. Transient pre-noise data is read but not applied.
- **`filmcraft-codecs`**: E-AC-3 in MP4/MOV, Matroska and TS now goes to the decoder. `FixedFrames::Eac3` counts packet samples across the syncframes of an access unit.
- **`filmcraft-mpegts`**: the ES splitter now joins dependent-substream frames to the access unit of the independent frame before them, as MP4 and Matroska do, so TS timing stays right for 7.1.

## Tests
- `ac3/tests/oracle.rs`: 5 ffmpeg-encoded raw E-AC-3 streams (stereo, 64k coupling + rematrixing, mono 32 kHz, 5.1+LFE with bsi metadata, noise). SNR vs ffmpeg is 64.8–91.0 dB, the same order as…

title: #780: Optical Flow time interpolation synthesises motion-compensated frames
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G18 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #780.

## Problem
A speed-changed clip with Time Interpolation set to **Optical Flow** rendered exactly like **Frame Blending**: a cross-fade of the two neighbouring source frames, so moving objects showed up twice (the old `TODO(optical flow)` on `interpolation_blend`). Premiere builds the in-between frame from the motion, so a moving object shows up once, where it should be at that moment.

## Fix
New module `crates/render/src/flow.rs` (CPU, pure Rust, deterministic). It uses only textbook methods, written from the published equations:
1. **Dense flow:** Lucas–Kanade solved at every pixel, with window sums done by a box filter. It is Gauss–Newton iterated with bilinear warping, Tikhonov-damped at a gradient noise floor so flat areas keep the coarser estimate, and run coarse to fine over a binomial luma pyramid at most 640 px wide. Larger frames are box-reduced first, and the flow is scaled back up. After each level, motion is dropped wherever standing still matches the window as well, so flicker or lights switching on static content is not read as motion. A 3×3 median follows. The flow is computed both ways.
2. **Flow at the in-between time:** both flows are forward-splatted to time t, after the interpolation in Baker et al., IJCV 2011. When two pixels land on the same spot, the one that is forward–backward consistent and photometrically better wins. Holes are filled from their neighbours.
3. **Warp and blend:** frame 0 is fetched at `x − t·u` and frame 1 at `x + (1−t)·u`. Each fetch is weighted by `(1−t, t)` times how well that pixel's own flow agrees with `u`, so background an object uncovers comes from the frame that shows it. Pixels that look the same in both frames, or where neither fetch agrees, fade to the plain cross-fade.

`media_image` calls `flow::interpolate` for `TimeInterpolation::OpticalFlow` clips, and Frame Blending is unchanged. Inputs are treated as hostile: size mismatches, empty or short buffers, NaN or ∞ pixe…

title: #779: export JPEG, Targa and DPX image sequences
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G13 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #779.

## Problem
Premiere Pro offers JPEG, Targa and DPX as image-sequence export formats. FilmCraft only wrote PNG, TIFF and BMP sequences.

## Fix
- Three new `Format`s: `jpg` (JPEG sequence), `tga` (Targa sequence), `dpx` (DPX sequence). They are numbered like the existing sequences (`Shot000.dpx` …) and available from the export dialog, CLI, control channel and MCP. Each has a built-in preset under *Image Sequence*.
- JPEG: encoded with the `image` crate at `ExportSettings::quality`. The export UI shows the Quality slider for it, as it does for Motion JPEG. The id `jpeg` still means Motion JPEG, so existing scripts keep working.
- Targa (TGA 2.0) and DPX (SMPTE ST 268): a small writer written from the public specs, in `crates/export/src/raster.rs`. Targa is uncompressed with a bottom-left origin: 24-bit, or 32-bit straight alpha with *Include Alpha Channel*. DPX is 10-bit RGB (8-bit values widened by bit replication), packed into 32-bit big-endian words (method A), and tagged BT.709. Sizes are checked; bad buffers or sizes return errors instead of panicking.
- `Format::is_image_sequence` replaces the format lists that were kept by hand in settings and automation. The size estimate, summary, presets and es/ja/zh-cn catalog entries are updated.
- Docs: G13 section of `docs/gaps.md`, the matching rows of `file-format-parity.md`, and the export table in `architecture.md`.

## Tests
- `settings_tests::jpeg_targa_and_dpx_sequences`: exports 3 frames of a half-transparent blue matte in each new format. It checks the file names and sizes, checks that quality 95 gives a bigger JPEG than quality 20, and decodes every first still with ffmpeg (external oracle; skipped when ffmpeg is absent). title: #790: Matroska AAC / MP3 / AC-3 trims the exact CodecDelay
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #790.

## Problem
ffmpeg stores the encoder priming as `CodecDelay` in nanoseconds (1024 AAC samples at 48 kHz = 21.333 ms, 256 AC-3 samples at 44.1 kHz = 5.805 ms, 1105 MP3 samples = 25.057 ms) and block timestamps in whole milliseconds. The demuxer subtracts the delay rounded to 1 ms, and for AAC, MPEG audio and AC-3 the packet starts were anchored on that rounded timestamp, so the whole track played 16 samples (AAC 48 kHz), 10 (AAC 44.1 kHz) or 8 (AC-3 44.1 kHz) late against ffmpeg's decode. Only Opus undid the rounding.

## Fix
`crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs`: one timestamp-to-samples conversion (`stamp_to_samples`) for every Matroska audio codec. It undoes the demuxer's rounded delay and removes the exact `CodecDelay` (`codec_delay_samples`, rounded to the nearest sample, since the element holds whole ns: 21 333 333 ns for 1024 samples at 48 kHz). Opus now uses the same helper. Checked/saturating math guards against hostile timebases and delays. Tracks without `CodecDelay` behave exactly as before.

## Tests
- `audio_timing_tests::matroska_codec_delay_is_trimmed_to_the_sample` (unit test, no ffmpeg): AAC from our own encoder, muxed with `CodecDelay` at 48 and 44.1 kHz, must equal the back-to-back decode with exactly 1024 samples trimmed. Fails without the fix (all samples shifted).
- `tests/matroska_audio_oracle.rs::matroska_audio_is_sample_aligned_with_ffmpeg` (ffmpeg oracle, skips without ffmpeg): pink noise as AAC 48k/44.1k, AC-3 44.1k/48k and MP3 44.1k in MKV. Our decode must line up with ffmpeg's at lag 0, and a read from the middle must match continuous decoding. Before the fix: AAC 48 kHz was −16.

## Gates
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -j 4 -p filmcraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -j 4 -p filmcraft-codecs` (full suite, all targets green), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p filmcraft-codecs --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Full `cargo xtask ci` not run locally (shared machine).

title: Timeline: Option-drag copies clips instead of moving them
author: impostazioni
body:
## Problem
Holding Option (Alt) while dragging a clip in the Timeline moved the clip, the same as a plain drag. In Premiere, Option-drag duplicates: the original stays where it is and a copy lands where the pointer lets go.

## Fix
- **edit:** `copy_items` places copies of the listed clips (overwrite or insert, like a move) and gives them new ids. Copies of linked clips are linked to each other, not to the originals. A copy whose partner isn't copied is unlinked. Transitions that would travel with a move are copied too.
- **engine:** `timeline.move` takes `copy: true`. The originals stay put, the copies are selected and returned as `copied`, and it's one undo step. Linked partners are copied unless `linked: false`. Destinations on a locked track are refused.
- **ui:** the move drag remembers whether Option is held, as of the last drag frame, so letting go of Option and the mouse together still copies. While Option is held:
  - the originals stay drawn in place;
  - the copies follow the pointer (automation ids `timeline.clip.<id>.copy`);
  - the cursor shows a copy.

  The drop sends `copy: true`. Cmd-drag (insert) works with Option-drag.
- **docs:** `docs/control-protocol.md` documents `copy`.

## Tests
- `timeline_move_tests::copy_leaves_the_originals_and_links_the_copies`: originals untouched; linked picture and sound copied with their offset; copies linked to each other only; selection; one undo; `linked: false`; refused on a locked track.
- `tests/timeline_option_drag_ui.rs` (headless): an Option-drag adds a copy and keeps the original, one undo removes it, and a plain drag still moves.

`cargo fmt`, clippy (`-D warnings`) and the edit / engine / ui-egui tests pass locally. The one failure on my machine, `export_tests::every_builtin_preset_exports_and_ffprobe_confirms` (APV 422-10), also fails on `main` because this machine's ffmpeg 7.1 has no APV.

title: #577: Effect Controls shows a selected transition's own timeline
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G8 (docs/gaps.md). Part of #577.

## Problem
With a transition selected, Effect Controls showed only its settings (Duration, Alignment, Reverse, its own parameters). Premiere shows the transition's own timeline beside them: clip A, clip B and the transition over their cut, where the transition can be slid over the cut or resized by dragging. In FilmCraft that was only possible in the Timeline. The rest of #577 (select / Delete a transition, drag its edge or middle in the Timeline, its settings in Effect Controls) already works on main.

## Fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/transition_controls.rs`: to the right of the settings, using the clip view's divider and saved width, there is now:
- a time ruler over the cut (sequence timecode, frame ticks when zoomed in)
- the outgoing clip (A) on top, the transition (outlined as selected) in the middle, the incoming clip (B) at the bottom, plus the cut line and the playhead
- **dragging the middle** of the transition slides it over the cut. **Dragging an end** changes its duration from that end while the other end stays put. These follow the Timeline's rules (`filmcraft_edit::transitions::drag_span`), clamped to the clips and the cut, in whole frames. A drag is measured against the view it started in, so the ruler stays still while the transition changes. Each drag is one undoable `sequence.setTransition` (`merge`/`begin`), and the Duration field and Program monitor update live.
- clicking or dragging the ruler moves the playhead.

The menu also needs to reflect colors customized through Preferences → Labels.

title: fix(playback): keep audio during forward shuttle speeds (#771)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Pressing L twice to shuttle forward at 2× speed stops audio playback.

This prevents editors from reviewing footage and listening to audio while shuttling forward.

## Root cause

The audio startup path explicitly disables audio whenever playback speed differs from 1×.

## Changes

- Allow audio playback during supported forward shuttle speeds.
- Calculate an effective audio mixing sample rate based on playback speed.
- Preserve the hardware device's actual sample rate and playback clock.
- Keep reverse playback and unsupported extreme speeds silent.
- Add regression coverage for 1×, 2×, 4×, and invalid playback speeds.

Audio at accelerated speeds uses the expected pitch-shifted playback rather than pitch-preserving time stretching.

## Validation

- Added `forward_shuttle_playback_keeps_audio_enabled`.
- Reviewed the committed source changes.
- Rust tests, formatting checks, and audible playback verification have not been executed.

## Issue

Addresses #771

title: #800: MP2 audio in MP4 and MOV decodes instead of playing silent
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #800.

## Problem
MP4 and QuickTime name MPEG audio without its layer: ffmpeg stores MP2 as `mp4a` + `esds` object type 0x6B (ffprobe even reports it as "mp3"). `PacketDecoder::for_isobmff` always made symphonia's layer III decoder for it, and that decoder rejects every frame of another layer (`mpa: invalid mpeg audio layer`), so MP2 in MP4 played as silence. In MOV, ffmpeg writes the QuickTime `.mp2` sample entry, which we did not recognise, so decoding failed.

## Fix
- `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`: MPEG audio from MP4 / MOV gets a decoder that is created on the first packet, for the layer that packet's frame header names (ISO/IEC 11172-3 §2.4.2.3; new `mpeg_audio_layer`). Same pattern as the existing lazy AAC decoder. A packet without a header gives an error, not a crash, and the next packet tries again.
- `crates/isobmff/src/codec.rs`: `.mp2` maps to `CodecConfig::Mp3` (MPEG audio of any layer), like `.mp3`.
- `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs`: layer I/II tracks are labelled "MPEG Audio", as Matroska's are, not "mp3".
- MP4 and MOV both carry an edit list that trims the 481-sample encoder delay, and we already honour it, so the decode now lines up with ffmpeg's with zero offset.

## Tests
- `audio::mpeg_audio_tests` (unit tests, no ffmpeg needed): layer parsing, including hostile and short headers; an MP4 MPEG-audio decoder decodes synthetic layer II and layer III frames. The layer II case **failed before** with `invalid mpeg audio layer`.
- `isobmff` `quicktime_mpeg_audio_entries`: `.mp2` and `.mp3` parse as MPEG audio, also under a handler other than `soun` (failed before for `.mp2`).
- `mp4_oracle::mp2_in_mp4_and_mov_matches_ffmpeg` (skips without ffmpeg): stereo MP2 in MP4 at 48 kHz and in MOV at 44.1 kHz matches ffmpeg's decode from the first sample, same length, also after a seek into the middle. Max error is 6e-7 for MP4; for MOV it is 3e-5, because ffmpeg decodes `.mp2` to s16. Failed before.

title: #805: Morph Cut morphs along optical flow instead of cross-dissolving
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G18 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #805.

## Problem
Morph Cut was a plain Cross Dissolve (`transitions/legacy.rs`), so a jump cut in a talking-head shot showed the subject twice at half opacity for the length of the transition. The GPU plan also treated it as a layer-mixable dissolve.

## Fix
- `transitions/dissolve.rs`: Morph Cut is `flow::interpolate(a, b, p)`: both frames warp along the dense optical flow between them (the coarse-to-fine Lucas–Kanade flow from #780 / #789) and blend, so the subject moves from its place in the outgoing shot to its place in the incoming one. Where the frames do not correspond, it stays the cross dissolve (the flow module's own fallback). Endpoints are still exactly A and B.
- `transitions/legacy.rs`: Morph Cut is no longer an alias of Cross Dissolve.
- `plan.rs`: Morph Cut is no longer a "simple" transition, so its frames are planned whole on the CPU (preview and export show the morph, not a GPU dissolve). `preview.rs` costs it as a complex transition.
- Morph Cut goldens re-blessed (those are the only changed lines). Docs: G18 section and the effects line in `target-app-parity.md`.

## Tests
- `transitions::tests::morph_cut_moves_the_subject_instead_of_double_exposing`: a 12 px jump. At the midpoint the subject is drawn once, 6 px along. Column errors are checked in the uncovered band, at both edges, in the middle and in the band still to be covered, where the dissolve ghosts by more than 0.3. The overall error is more than 10× lower than the dissolve's, and the background is left alone.
- `transitions::tests::morph_cut_tracks_textured_subjects_and_follows_the_progress`: a textured subject on a textured background, at p = 0.5 and p = 0.25. The error is less than half the dissolve's.
- `tests::morph_cut_frames_render_on_the_cpu_with_the_morph`: frames inside the transition are CPU frames and match `render_sequence`. Frames outside it stay on the GPU.
- The existing transition property tests still pass for Morph Cut: exact endpoints…

title: #806: export OpenEXR image sequences
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G13 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #806.

## Problem
Premiere offers OpenEXR as an image-sequence export format; FilmCraft could not write EXR at all.

## Fix
- New export format `exr` ("OpenEXR", also accepts `openexr`) writing numbered `.exr` stills like the other sequences, with an "OpenEXR Sequence" preset, the Include Alpha Channel option (`supports_alpha`), the `file.exportMedia` format list, bitrate estimate / summary, and es/ja/zh-cn strings.

Values are scene-linear (the pipeline's sRGB/709 curve undone via `filmcraft_color::srgb_u8_to_linear_table`) and alpha is premultiplied, as EXR defines. f32 to half conversion rounds to nearest even. Hostile sizes are errors (checked math, `i32` window / chunk-size limits).
- No new dependency. ZIP / PIZ / DWA compression is left open (ZIP would need a deflate encoder).

- `raster::tests::half_floats_round_to_nearest_even` (normals, subnormals, ties, overflow, NaN).

title: #813: masks round their corners (rounded rectangle masks)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G18 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #813.

## Problem
Premiere 26's redesigned mask tools give rectangle masks rounded corners. FilmCraft masks (ellipse, 4-point polygon, pen) could only have sharp corners.

## Fix
- `filmcraft-project`: `MaskPath::with_rounded_corners(radius, corners)` replaces each sharp corner between two straight edges by a circular fillet: two vertices on the edges joined by a cubic arc with handles `4/3·tan(φ/4)·r` (a right angle gets the usual KAPPA quarter circle). The fillet shrinks so it never takes more than half of either edge. `roundable_corners()` lists the corners it can round, and `rounded_rect(...)` builds a rounded rectangle. Hostile input is safe: NaN, infinite or negative radii and out-of-range or repeated indices are clamped or ignored. A degenerate corner (straight, reversing, zero-length edge) still becomes two coincident vertices, so vertex counts stay equal across keyframes.
- `filmcraft-engine`: `masks.add` takes `"cornerRadius": px` for rectangle/polygon shapes. The new `masks.roundCorners` command (`{"radius": px, "vertices": [n]?}`) rounds an existing mask's corners, or only the listed vertices, in one undo step. It applies the same corners to every Mask Path keyframe so animated paths keep interpolating. It returns `{"corners": n}`, and errors when the radius is ≤ 0 or there is nothing to round.
- Docs: G18 section of `docs/gaps.md`, the masks paragraph of `docs/architecture.md`.

## Tests
- `mask::tests::rounded_rect_corners_are_quarter_circles`: flattened corners lie on radius-r circles about the inset centres, edges stay straight, the corner is cut away, radius 0 = plain rect.
- `mask::tests::rounding_clamps_to_half_an_edge_and_ignores_curves_and_hostile_input`: an oversized radius gives a stadium (fillets meet at edge midpoints), a triangle, an ellipse (nothing to round), NaN/∞/negative radii, bad indices, collinear vertices.
- `masks_tests::rounded_rectangle_masks_cut_their_corners`: a rendered rounded opacity mask c…

title: #809: own MPEG audio Layer I / II decoder plays MP2 at ffmpeg's default bit rates
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #809.

## Problem
symphonia rejects every Layer II frame whose bit rate / channel mode combination ISO/IEC 11172-3 does not allow: mono above 192 kbit/s and stereo below 64 kbit/s (`mpa: invalid Layer 2 bitrate for mono channel mode`; 0.5.5, still in 0.6). ffmpeg writes mono MP2 at **384 kbit/s by default**, so such tracks played as silence in MPEG-TS / PS, Matroska and raw `.mp2` files (and in MP4 / MOV once #808 lands).

## Fix
- New L0 crate `crates/mpa` (`filmcraft-mpa`, depends only on `filmcraft-bitstream` + `thiserror`, no `unsafe`, wasm32 clean): a clean-room MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer I and Layer II decoder written from ISO/IEC 11172-3 (§2.4 syntax and decoding, Annex B tables) and ISO/IEC 13818-3 (lower sampling frequencies). No FFmpeg / libmad / mpg123 / twolame source consulted.
  - Layer I and II, mono / stereo / dual channel / joint (intensity) stereo at every bound, MPEG-1, MPEG-2 LSF and MPEG-2.5, with or without CRC.
  - Lenient like encoders: the Layer II allocation table is chosen by sampling frequency and bit rate per channel with Table 3-B.2's ranges taken as open-ended, so the disallowed combinations decode the way ffmpeg writes them.
  - Free format and Layer III are refused with `Unsupported` (Layer III stays with symphonia). Every input-derived index goes through `get()`; errors, never panics.
- `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`:
  - `PacketDecoder::mpeg_audio` uses it for layers I and II (MPEG-TS / PS / ES, Matroska `A_MPEG/L2`); a packet may hold several frames. #808's `lazy_mpeg_audio` calls `mpeg_audio(layer, …)`, so MP4 / MOV pick it up when #808 is merged. I kept my lines away from #808's hunks in `audio.rs`. The doc lines in `gaps.md` / `codec-parity.md` overlap, so whichever PR merges second needs a trivial doc rebase.
  - Raw `.mp2` files (`AudioFileSource`) whose stream starts with a Layer I / II frame (after an optional ID3v2 tag) decode with our decoder and resync after damage. MP3 and anything else still g…

title: monitors: the wheel zooms about the pointer, the middle button pans
author: ReReddo
body:
Closes #807.

Zooming a monitor took the zoom dropdown, which zooms about the middle of the picture, and then scrolling or the Hand tool to bring the part you wanted into view. At Fit the wheel did nothing. Now, on the Program and Source monitors:

- **The mouse wheel zooms about the pointer**, from Fit too: the point under the pointer stays under it, so you zoom straight into the part you're working on. A trackpad pinch zooms the same way. The zoom stays between the dropdown's 10% and 1600%, and the dropdown shows the current percentage.
- **A middle-button drag pans** the zoomed picture, whatever tool is active. The Hand tool still pans with the left button.
- **Fit resets** zoom and pan, and each monitor keeps its own zoom and pan, as before.
- Comparison View, which always fits both frames, ignores the wheel.

The wheel used to pan a zoomed picture; panning is now the middle button's and the Hand tool's job.

**Changes**

- `panels/monitor_view.rs`: `pan_input` becomes `zoom_pan_input`. The wheel or a pinch scales the zoom about the pointer and sets the pan so the point under it stays, clamped like any pan. A middle-button press over the picture starts a pan that follows the pointer until the button comes up.
- `panels/timeline.rs`: `wheel_input` and `WheelInput` are shared (`pub(crate)`), so the monitors read the wheel the same way the Timeline does (lines and pages in points, the events' own modifiers, pinches) and zoom at the same speed, 1% per point of wheel travel.

title: #814: AAC Audio export (audio-only .m4a, or ADTS .aac)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G13 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #814.

## Problem
Premiere / Media Encoder offer an "AAC Audio" format (the mix alone, as AAC). FilmCraft wrote AAC only inside H.264 / H.265 / AV1 movies; the only audio-only exports were Waveform Audio and AIFF.

## Fix
- New export format `aac` ("AAC Audio", `Format::Aac`, extension `.m4a`). It encodes the sequence mix with the existing AAC-LC encoder (the registered audio encoder factories, so a platform encoder can take it) into an MPEG-4 file with only an audio track, the encoder delay in an edit list, the same as the audio in our MP4 exports. A path ending in `.aac` writes a raw ADTS stream instead (7-byte headers, no CRC, fields read from the AudioSpecificConfig; configurations ADTS cannot signal return an error instead of writing a bad file).
- Bitrate, sample rate, mono / stereo / 5.1 and loudness normalisation come from the existing audio settings. Export mode needs no new code: the format list comes from `Format::ALL`, and audio-only formats already hide the video sections and show the AAC bitrate row.
- New `Format::is_audio_only()` replaces the `Wav | Aiff` checks in settings. New Audio Only preset "AAC Audio 48 kHz 320 kbps". `file.exportMedia` keeps a `.aac` path, and the CLI guesses `aac` from `.m4a` / `.aac`. Added es / fr / ja / zh-cn strings.
- Docs: G13 and file-format-parity updated, plus a row in the architecture export table. G13 also drops "ProRes 4444 / XQ in the export UI": the Export mode ProRes profile combo already offers both (#342 is closed).

Overlap with #812 (OpenEXR): textual conflicts only in `docs/gaps.md` and the `file.exportMedia` param string in `commands.rs`. Both PRs change `Format::ALL: [Format; 18]` to `19` (and the `ALL.len() == 18` test). Git merges that cleanly because the line is the same, but whichever lands second has to bump it to 20.

## Tests

title: #821: import Targa and DPX stills and image sequences
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #821.

## Problem
Premiere imports Targa (`.tga`) and DPX (`.dpx`) as stills and as numbered image sequences. FilmCraft exports both (#779) but could not import either: the extensions were not in the importable still list and the `image` crate has no DPX reader, so even FilmCraft's own Targa / DPX renders could not be brought back in.

## Fix
Clean-room decoders in `filmcraft-media`, no new dependencies:
- **`tga.rs`** (Truevision TGA 2.0 spec): image types 1/2/3 and their RLE forms 9/10/11 (packets may span lines), colour maps with 15/16/24/32-bit entries indexed by 8 or 16 bits, 15/16-bit 5-5-5 (alpha bit when the descriptor says so), 24-bit BGR, 32-bit BGRA, 8-bit grayscale, 16-bit grayscale + alpha, any origin corner. Sniffed by the TGA 2.0 footer, or a `.tga` name plus a plausible header (the original format has no magic). A 32-bit file whose alpha is zero everywhere and whose descriptor declares no attribute bits is shown opaque (a common writer bug).
- **`dpx.rs`** (SMPTE ST 268): first image element; luma / RGB / RGBA / ABGR; 8 and 16-bit; 10-bit filled into 32-bit words (method A and B); 12-bit in 16-bit words (method A and B); `SDPX` and `XPDS` byte orders; 32-bit line alignment plus end-of-line padding; orientations 0–3. RLE, packed (packing 0) 10/12-bit, Y'CbCr, float and transposed orientations return an "unsupported" error.
- Both cap the picture at 16384² pixels and check the data is present (RLE: against the most a packet can expand to) before allocating. Malformed headers return errors, never panic.
- `still::decode_raster` is the one decode entry point for stills and image sequences (`ImageSequenceSource` now also uses `get()` instead of indexing its frame list). `tga` and `dpx` join `STILL_EXTENSIONS`, so the Media Browser, import dialogs and sequence detection pick them up.
- Frames stay RGBA8 like every other still (16-bit PNG/TIFF included): deeper DPX values are rounded to 8 bits.
- Docs: G10 in `docs/gaps.md`…

title: #820: fall back to DX12, then a software adapter, when the graphics start fails
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G4 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #820.

## Problem
A graphics driver that crashes inside wgpu instance or device creation (Intel's Vulkan driver `igvk64.dll`, #512 #413 #793; AMD's `atio6axx.dll`, #477; Windows reports #582) kills the app on every launch the same way, before any Rust error handling runs. The only fix was setting `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` by hand. A start-up error wgpu does report (no adapter, device creation failed) ended in the error dialog.

## Fix
`apps/filmcraft/src/graphics.rs`:
- Each start writes a marker to the data folder (`graphics-start.json`, `{"mode", "pending"}`, written to a temp file and renamed). It is cleared once the window has painted two frames (an egui `on_end_pass` hook), or when the app closes normally.
- If the marker is still pending at the next launch, that start died, so this launch uses the next mode on the platform's ladder and keeps it: Windows `default` (Vulkan+DX12, no GL as before), then `dx12`, then `software` (WARP, DX12 only); Linux `default`, then `software` (lavapipe / llvmpipe through Vulkan or GL, picked by a `native_adapter_selector`); macOS only `default`. Software mode composites on the CPU through the existing `set_wgpu` software-rasterizer check.
- If `eframe::run_native` returns `Error::Wgpu` before the app was created, the next mode is tried in the same process (eframe reuses its event loop).
- Fallback modes don't register the GPU export renderer, because its own `Instance::default()` would load the driver that failed. Exports then composite on the CPU.
- An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` leaves the marker alone. A missing, corrupt or oversized marker (reads are capped at 4 KiB) starts in the default mode.
- `main.rs`: the window options and the app creator are now functions, so a retry can build them again (`Launch` derives `Clone`). The existing error dialog is still shown when every mode fails.

## Tests
New `graphics::tests`: the ladder transitions (a pending start moves on, a confirmed one is kept, the end of…

title: Codecs: AV1 NVENC export, decoding hardening, and pipeline error handling
author: AnarchByte0
body:
This PR updates FilmCraft's AV1 codec and export path, plus shared decoder error handling used by the codec pipeline.

- Adds Windows NVIDIA NVENC AV1 Main and Main 10 export for MP4/MOV, including PQ/HLG color signaling, static HDR metadata, sequence-header-derived av1C, and export UI availability.
- Hardens the pure-Rust AV1 decoder against oversized allocations and worker/parser panics, and propagates delayed decode failures through flush and the GOP cache.
- Keeps Linux NVENC HEVC disabled, preserving upstream's revert in f114b5f1. AV1 NVENC is Windows-only. Software AV1 encoding remains unsupported.

Validation on Windows with an RTX 5070 (FFmpeg/ffprobe used only as external test oracles):
- AV1, codecs, and export all-target tests passed, including hostile-stream and size tests.
- Platform unit tests and NVENC regressions passed; six SDR/PQ/HLG MP4/MOV exports were externally decoded and reopened/searched in FilmCraft.
- Media Foundation AV1 8/10-bit tests, 20 extended conformance vectors against libdav1d, and the ignored 1080p inter test passed.
- Workspace release Clippy with -D warnings, formatting, layers, assets, and WASM passed.

Full workspace CI has not completed: cargo xtask ci stopped during workspace release test compilation while building the full application and test suite. Treat the check as pending. A broader test run on the earlier local checkout also found a VP9 profile-2 Media Foundation reset issue (one missing PTS); AV1 cases passed.

title: Clear Close Sequence also clears File Close (Cmd+W)
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #773.

File ▸ Close (`file.close`, Cmd+W) aliases Close Sequence (`sequence.close`). Clear in the Keyboard editor sent Application on `sequence.close`, which only had a Timeline chord, so Application Cmd+W stayed on `file.close`.

`file.close` and `sequence.close` now share shortcut bindings. Clear on either removes every chord in the pair.

`clear_close_sequence_also_clears_file_close` covers this.

title: OS drops on an empty Timeline create a sequence
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #785.

OS file drops already imported into the Project bin. They were only placed on the Timeline when a sequence was already open and the pointer was in the clip area. On an empty project the Timeline empty state never consumed the pending drop.

Dropping media on the empty Timeline now creates a sequence from the first imported item (`file.newSequence` `fromItem`) and places any extra items. `drop_import_to_timeline` still gates this.

title: #828: import OpenEXR stills and image sequences
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #828.

## Problem
FilmCraft can export OpenEXR sequences (#806) but could not open `.exr` files: EXR plates, CG renders and VFX returns from other apps could not be imported as stills or image sequences.

## Fix
- New clean-room OpenEXR reader `crates/media/src/still/exr.rs` (from the public OpenEXR file layout): single-part scan-line files, compression none / RLE / ZIPS / ZIP, half / float / uint channels. R, G, B, A become the frame (missing colour channels 0, missing alpha opaque); luminance-only (Y) files show grey.
- EXR is scene-linear with premultiplied alpha, which is exactly the compositor's working format, so frames are `PixelData::RgbaF32` with `Transfer::Linear` (values above 1.0 survive into effects and colour work; the render path already handles float frames).
- Data window placed into the display window (overscan cut, uncovered area transparent).
- ZIP needs inflate: our own zlib / DEFLATE decoder (`still/exr/inflate.rs`, RFC 1950/1951, table-driven), so **no new dependency**.
- Hooks: `pub mod exr;` in `still.rs`, an EXR branch at the top of `open_bytes`, `"exr"` in `STILL_EXTENSIONS`, and `sequence.rs` decodes frames through a small `decode_frame` helper (EXR → float frame, everything else unchanged).
- Refused with a clear `Unsupported` error: tiled, deep, multi-part, chroma-subsampled (RY/BY) files and PIZ / PXR24 / B44 / DWA compression. Hostile input (truncation, bad offsets, oversized windows, corrupt zlib/RLE) returns errors, never panics; sizes are capped (2^26 pixels).
- A 4K ZIP half RGBA frame decodes in ~160 ms (rayon over chunks).

Rebased onto main after #826 (Targa / DPX import) merged: non-EXR sequence frames still go through its `still::decode_raster`.

## Tests
- Unit (`still/exr/tests.rs`, `still/exr/inflate.rs`): half conversion (incl. subnormals / inf / NaN); RGBA half under every compression (hand-built files, two ZIP chunks with a partial one) decoding identically; luminance-only; extra channe…

title: AV1: reserve API for a future software encoder
author: AnarchByte0
body:
The local software AV1 prototype does not encode input pixels into a conformant stream. This draft preserves the work for review while exposing only a safe reserved API: invalid configurations return Invalid, and valid construction, encoding and flushing return Unsupported.

The unfinished OBU/header, entropy-coding, prediction and transform fragments are kept in crates/av1enc/prototype/, outside the compiled src tree. The crate is registered as L0 in workspace metadata and the WASM/layer checks. It is not registered in the export pipeline and does not provide software AV1 export. Hardware AV1 export is covered separately by #829.

Before enabling software encoding, the implementation needs pixel reconstruction and bitstream conformance, GOP/seek and bitrate checks, and hostile-input regressions against external test oracles. The README records AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification v1.0.0 with Errata 1 as the intended clean-room specification.

Validation:
- All 3 filmcraft-av1enc tests pass, covering hostile configurations, dimension boundaries and Unsupported behavior.
- Workspace release Clippy (-D warnings), formatting, layers, assets (69 attributed assets), and WASM (45 crates) pass.
- Full workspace CI was attempted but stopped during workspace release test compilation. Its result remains unverified.

title: Paste cut clips even when old OS clipboard files linger
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #697.

After Copy/Cut, FilmCraft puts clip names on the OS clipboard, but many platforms still hold a previous file list. Paste preferred that media (`edit.pasteMedia`) over the session clip clipboard, so Cmd+V / Ctrl+V (and Edit ▸ Paste) did not paste the cut clips.

On a successful copy/cut, the current OS files/image are snapshotted. Paste ignores that same media and pastes the clips. New files or an image copied afterward still import as before (#611).

Covered in `clipboard_paste_ui` plus existing `ctrl_c_and_ctrl_v_copy_and_paste_clips`.

title: #841: import packed 10/12-bit and Y'CbCr DPX stills
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G10 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #841.

## Problem
DPX import (#821) rejected two layouts with an "unsupported" error: 10/12-bit components in the "packed" layout (packing 0), and the Y'CbCr descriptors (100 CbYCrY 4:2:2, 101 CbYACrYA 4:2:2:4, 102 CbYCr 4:4:4, 103 CbYCrA 4:4:4:4).

## Fix
All changes are in `crates/media/src/dpx.rs`, written from SMPTE ST 268:
- **Packed (packing 0):** components follow each other with no padding, starting in the low bits of a 32-bit word. A component that crosses into the next word continues in that word's low bits, and each scan line starts on a 32-bit boundary. ffmpeg reads 12-bit packed files the same way (checked against it below). This works in both byte orders.
- **Y'CbCr:** converted to RGB with `filmcraft_color::ycbcr_to_rgb`.
  - Matrix: taken from the colorimetric field. Codes 5 and 6 mean BT.709; codes 7–10 (601 and composite video) mean BT.601. When the field is unspecified, `filmcraft_frame::default_matrix` picks by picture size.
  - Range: video range, unless the reference low / high data codes cover the full code range (0 and the maximum code value).
  - 4:2:2: both pixels of a pair use the pair's chroma. With an odd width, the last pixel has no Cr, so it gets neutral chroma.
  - Alpha (101, 103) is kept straight.
- Run-length encoded DPX is still unsupported.

## Tests
- `dpx.rs` unit tests:
  - packed 10-bit components that cross word boundaries, in both byte orders, and packed 12-bit;
  - CbYCrY in BT.709 and BT.601;
  - full-range 10-bit CbYCr;
  - 16-bit CbYCrA with alpha;
  - 8-bit CbYACrYA with an odd width.
- Hostile-header cases updated: unknown descriptor, unsupported packing, truncated packed data.
- New ffmpeg oracle test `codecs/tests/media_oracle.rs::dpx_packed_and_ycbcr_match_ffmpeg`. ffmpeg reads these layouts but cannot write them, so the test builds the files from ffmpeg's test picture:
  - packed 12-bit RGB at 95 × 63, so lines need padding;
  - 8-bit CbYCrY and CbYCr, each with colorimetric codes…

title: number fields: type a calculation and get its result
author: ReReddo
body:
Closes #817.

A number field took only a plain number; anything else was thrown away and the old value stayed. Now every number field takes a calculation and applies its result when you press Enter or click away:

- **`100*2` gives 200, `1920/3` gives 640, `(50+10)*1.5` gives 90.** `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` (also `×` and `÷`), brackets, decimals and negative numbers.
- **Applied to the current value:** the blue drag values now open with their value selected, so typing `*2` doubles it and `/3` divides it by three. Press End first to add to the value instead (`200/3`). `+` and `-` at the start stay signs, so `-10` is minus ten.
- **Units can be typed or left out:** `50%*2` and `1920 px / 2` work.
- **Bad input changes nothing:** something that isn't a calculation, a division by zero, or letters between digits (`1e3`, `10x20`, refused rather than read as 13 or 1020) leave the value as it was. A result outside the field's range is clamped, as a typed number is today.

It covers the blue drag values (Effect Controls, Properties, Lumetri, the Audio Track and Clip Mixers) and the number fields of dialogs and Settings (Speed/Duration, Audio Gain, Sequence Settings, Export, transitions, graphics templates, voice-over and the rest).

- `widgets.rs`:
  - `hot_number` evaluates the typed text with `calc::eval` against the value it shows (its own unit is taken out first), and opens with the whole value selected.
  - New `number_drag`: an egui `DragValue` whose parser is `calc::eval` against the value it holds. The dialogs' and Settings' 30 `DragValue::new` calls use it.
- `panels/transition_controls.rs`: the duration field still reads a frame count, then timecode (`1.00` stays a second there), and only then a calculation in frames (`48/2`).

title: #480: exports no longer stop for good when a clip's decoding uses rayon (rotated iPhone HEVC clips)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #480 (closed when #662 was merged; #662 was reverted).

## Second version of #662

#662 was reverted because its regression test failed in the full (debug) test run: the stand-in decoder in the test summed with `.sum()`, which overflows. That panics in debug builds, and the cache then reported `Decode("internal error while decoding")`. It now wraps explicitly (`reduce(|| 0, u64::wrapping_add)`). The fix itself is unchanged, apart from being re-applied on current `main`: `frame_late_locked` now starts at `decode_start` (commit 45f2b8e2, open GOPs), and the split into `decode_until` keeps that. I had run the gates only with `--release`; this time they ran exactly as `CLAUDE.md` lists them (debug).

- The test passes in debug (3 of 3, 0.3 s).
- With the fix switched off, it still deadlocks in debug (2 of 2, 120 s watchdog).

## What was wrong

Reproduced with the three public iPhone files from the issue (sha256 checked) on current `main`, Linux, 16 threads: the 3-clip export stopped making frames in 5 of 16 runs, and in 7 of 14 more runs later. The process stayed alive at 0 % CPU with the output file no longer growing.

A thread dump at the stall (`gdb`, export run under it) shows it is not the HEVC decoder's frame threads (they are idle) but a deadlock in the frame cache (`GopCache`) on the global rayon pool:

- 15 export frame jobs (`Pipeline::frame` on rayon) wait in `GopCache::frame_late` for the cache's lock.
- The lock holder is in `GopCache::store` → `VideoFrame::rotated` → `rotate_plane`, which splits the rotation over rayon (`par_chunks_mut`). It waits in `join` for a piece another worker took.
- That worker, while waiting inside the piece, picked up another frame job asking the same cache for a frame, and blocks on the lock. The piece the holder waits for is under it on that worker's stack.

Each waits for the other, for good. The iPhone clips trigger it because their display rotation (-90°) is applied to every decoded frame under the cache's lock. The …

title: #840: restart an audio stream the device drops instead of playing silent
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G17 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #840.

## Problem
`apps/filmcraft/src/audio.rs` marked the cpal stream failed on its first error of any kind. `played_frames()` then returned `None`, and the UI stopped audio and played the rest of the playback without sound ("Audio output failed"). cpal's ALSA backend reports transient errors through the error callback and keeps the stream alive: spurious poll returns, short writes, and `alsa::poll() returned POLLERR` after an xrun, after which it stops calling back. Users see a second or two of audio, then silence while the meters keep moving (#23; #602 and #605 may be the same thing).

## Fix
- New `AudioOut::recover()`, a no-op by default. The UI calls it every frame during timeline and Source Monitor playback, before reading the clock.
- `CpalOut` keeps the play-ahead mixer in an `Arc<Mutex<..>>` shared with the stream, so a new stream picks up where the old one stopped. A small `Watchdog` restarts the stream:
  - at once on `DeviceNotAvailable`, using the configured device, or the default/fallback if that device is gone;
  - after a backend error, only if no samples were consumed for 300 ms (well under the UI's 1 s `AUDIO_STALL_S`).
  The restarted stream keeps the played-frame clock and must keep the same sample rate and channel count, because the mixer was built for them. At most 3 restarts in 10 s; after that, or if the restart fails, playback falls back to the wall clock without sound, as before.
- An error while samples keep flowing no longer silences playback.
- The device callback runs the mixer under `catch_unwind`. If the mixer panics, the callback plays silence and fails the stream instead of killing the audio thread. If the mixer is busy, the callback plays silence and does not advance the clock.

## Tests
- `apps/filmcraft` (`audio::tests`):
  - errors are sorted correctly (lost device vs backend error) and do not fail the stream;
  - an error while frames keep advancing is never restarted;
  - an error followed by…

title: #850: launch files open whatever the extension's case, with absolute paths
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G9 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #850.

## Problem
- `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs` picked the project among the launch files with `f.ends_with(".fcproj")`. Windows file associations and the shared-mime-info glob match extensions case-insensitively, so double-clicking `CUT.FCPROJ` started FilmCraft, which then tried to import the project as a media file.
- Launch paths were used as given. `filmcraft clip.mp4` stored `clip.mp4` in the project, and `filmcraft cut.fcproj` put `cut.fcproj` in Recent Projects. Both went missing once the app ran from another folder (desktop launcher, Open Most Recent).
- Both apps read `std::env::args()`, which panics on an argument that is not Unicode (for example a Latin-1 file name on Linux). The desktop app died before its window opened.
- `filmcraft-cli import` made paths absolute with `std::fs::canonicalize`. On Windows that returns verbatim `\\?\C:\...` paths, which ended up in the project. It also resolved symlinks.

## Fix
- `args::project_and_media` returns the project to open (the first file whose extension is `fcproj` in any case) and the media files to import. Every path goes through `args::absolute`, which uses `std::path::absolute`: no verbatim prefix, symlinks kept, and a path it cannot resolve is kept as given. `main.rs` uses this instead of its two `ends_with` filters.
- `args::parse` takes `OsString`s from `std::env::args_os()`. Options and file names are read lossily, so a non-Unicode file name is reported missing by the import instead of crashing. `--data-dir` keeps the folder exactly.
- `filmcraft-cli` reads `args_os()` lossily, and `import` uses `std::path::absolute` instead of `canonicalize`.

## Tests
- `apps/filmcraft` `args::tests`:
  - `a_project_is_recognised_whatever_the_case_of_its_extension`
  - `launch_files_are_made_absolute_and_split_case_insensitively`
  - `arguments_that_are_not_unicode_still_start_the_app` (unix: non-UTF-8 file name and `--data-dir`)

title: #853: Shift constrains pen mask segments to 45° steps
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G18 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #853.

## Problem
The Program monitor's pen mask tool ignored Shift, so straight horizontal, vertical or diagonal mask edges could not be drawn precisely. Premiere 26.0's redesigned mask tools constrain lines with Shift.

While testing this I hit a related bug: `masks::path_from_json` tried serde first. Serde also accepts the `{"p","in","out"}` vertex form (the one `masks.list` returns and the pen commits through `masks.add`), but it silently drops the unknown `in`/`out` keys. So a pen mask's dragged-out curves were committed as corners, and so was any `path` with tangents sent to `masks.add`/`masks.set` over the CLI, MCP or control channel.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/masks.rs` (pen overlay only): while Shift is held, a new point snaps onto the nearest 45° ray from the previous point. The snap happens in screen space, so it matches what you see, and the distance along the ray is kept. The rubber-band preview line follows the snap, and a Shift-drag also constrains the Bézier handle it pulls out. A small `constrain_45` helper sits after `open_polyline`. The diff stays away from the lines that #851 and #667 touch.
- `crates/engine/src/masks.rs`: `path_from_json` now parses the vertex forms first and only then falls back to the serialized `MaskPath`, which still parses.

## Tests
- `masks_ui::shift_constrains_pen_mask_segments_to_45_degrees` (headless egui harness, Shift held through the control channel): checks that the segments come out horizontal, vertical and horizontal, and that a Shift-dragged handle comes out horizontal. - `masks::tests::constrain_45_snaps_to_the_nearest_eighth_turn`: snaps to the axes and diagonals, and passes degenerate or NaN input through unchanged.

author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #854.

GIF delays are centiseconds, so 24 fps (41.67 ms) cannot be stored as a single delay. The exporter wrote 4 cs for every frame (96 frames of 4.0 s → 3.84 s). Delays are now distributed (4/4/5 cs) so they sum to the export range.

title: #854: GIF frame delays add up to the sequence duration
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #854.

## Problem
The GIF exporter built one `Delay` of `1000·den/num` ms and used it for every frame. GIF stores delays in whole centiseconds and the encoder truncates, so at 24 fps every 41.67 ms frame became 4 cs: a 4.0 s sequence played in 3.84 s (4 % fast). Other non-integer rates (23.976, 29.97, …) drifted the same way.

## Fix
`gif_delay_cs(rate, i)` in `crates/export/src/lib.rs` gives frame `i` the span from its rounded start time to the next frame's rounded start, so delays alternate (4, 4, 5, 4, 4, 4 cs at 24 fps) and add up to the exact duration. The math is checked i128 with clamping, which also replaces the old unchecked `(1000 * den) as u32` cast, so hostile rates can't panic or overflow.

## Tests
`tests::gif_frame_delays_add_up_to_the_duration` checks the 24 fps pattern, 30 frames at 29.97 fps summing to 100 cs, and hostile rates (0/0, `i64::MAX`). It then exports 24 frames at 24 fps as GIF, decodes it with `image`'s `GifDecoder`, and asserts the delays add up to 1000 ms. It fails without the fix (960 ms).

## Gates

- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-export --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: LongGOP seek / time-to-first-frame, not the H.264 throughput gap
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary

This PR is the **LongGOP seek / time-to-first-frame stall** from #848. It is **not** the ~3× per-core decode gap vs ffmpeg. SIMD, `-C target-cpu`, and pipelined entropy stay on the issue.

On real 4K camera files, decode was already ~10.5 ms vs a 40 ms budget. The ~460 ms tail was start-up: `preroll_ms` ≈ `lat.max`, one seek from the previous keyframe, tens of GOP cache misses, and evictions while walking the GOP. A later comment on #848 also noted that the preroll loop calls `schedule_playback`/`refresh`, so those frames were metered as on-clock latency.

## What changed

- **GOP cache eviction** now pins a window on the *requested* presentation timestamp, not the newest decoded picture. A frame-threaded burst past the playhead no longer drops the target and walks the GOP again.
- **Preroll** only schedules the frames that gate clock start (`PREROLL_FRAMES`), not a full prefetch run down a LongGOP.
- **`bench_playback`** reports queue→done latency only for jobs queued after the play clock; preroll/seek work stays in `preroll_ms`.

Bit-exact decode is unchanged (no SIMD, no `unsafe`, no decoder math).

## Tests

Synthetic long GOP: many pictures between the only sync sample; a burst decoder dumps more than `MIN_FRAMES` at once. Asserts the target stays cached, the decoder does not restart for the next frame, and asking for the first frame again does not walk the GOP twice.

## Out of scope

H.264 High 4:2:2 10-bit **decoder throughput** (~3× slower per core than ffmpeg). That still needs SIMD / target-cpu / pipelined entropy as discussed on #848.

title: #874: compressed (RLE / ZIPS / ZIP) OpenEXR export
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G13 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #874.

## Problem
OpenEXR sequences (#806) were written uncompressed only, because the workspace had no deflate encoder. The files come out 2–4x larger than they need to be, and Premiere offers a compression choice for EXR.

## Fix
- `crates/export/src/deflate.rs`: a small clean-room DEFLATE encoder (RFC 1951) inside a zlib wrapper (RFC 1950). It uses greedy LZ77 over a 32 KB window with bounded hash chains. Each block goes out as stored, fixed-Huffman or dynamic-Huffman, whichever is smallest. Huffman codes are length-limited and always complete. Worst case, the output is only the stored-block overhead larger than the input. No new dependency.
- `raster::exr` can now write RLE (1 line per chunk), ZIPS (1 line) and ZIP (16 lines). It applies the format's predictor first (even/odd byte interleave, then delta + 128). Any chunk that would not shrink is stored raw, as the format allows. Chunk sizes are checked against the i32 field limit.
- New `ExportSettings::exr_compression` (`none | rle | zips | zip`, serde default `none`). The default output is unchanged, and old settings and presets still load. I kept uncompressed as the default to stay conservative.
- New `exrCompression` param on `file.exportMedia`. Export mode gets a **Compression** combo for OpenEXR (automation id `export.video.exrCompression`), with es / fr / ja / zh-cn strings. The summary line and the size estimate both take the setting into account.
- docs/gaps.md G13 and file-format-parity.md now list RLE / ZIPS / ZIP as done.

## Tests
- `deflate::tests`: round trips through a minimal test-only inflater. Cases: empty input, tiny input, incompressible input (stored blocks), few-symbol input (dynamic), long repeats, multi-block input, and skewed frequencies. Also covers length limiting with a complete code (Kraft sum = 1) and the Adler-32 vector. title: h264: safe-SIMD 6-tap luma spike (decoder throughput half of #848)
author: vbasky
body:
# #848 decoder throughput: safe-SIMD 6-tap luma spike

## What this is

This is the **decoder throughput** half of #848 (scalar IDCT / interpolation vs ffmpeg SIMD — the ~3× per-core gap).

It is **not** the LongGOP seek / TTFF work. That lives in PR #876 (`fix/848-longgop-seek-preroll`) and is not redone here.

This PR is a **safe-SIMD spike of the 6-tap luma kernel** (`tap6` / `htap_row` / `vtap_row` in `crates/h264/src/inter.rs`). It is not a full SIMD port.

- No `unsafe`, no CPU intrinsics, no new ADR.
- No `-C target-cpu=native` (that remains packaging, not the ship default).
- Workspace still `forbid(unsafe_code)`. `wide` is a normal dependency (MIT/Apache/Zlib), same class as `rayon`.

## 6-tap in `wide`

**Yes — `wide` could express the 6-tap FIR.** The filter is `a − 5b + 20c + 20d − 5e + f` on `i32x8` (`wide` 0.7.33). Horizontal interpolation uses six overlapping 8-byte loads; vertical uses one load per of six rows. Widths 8 and 16 take the SIMD body; 4 and odd tails stay on the original scalar loop. SIMD and scalar are **bit-exact**.

`weighted_store` was **not** needed as a fallback.

## Tests

- `rtk cargo test -p filmcraft-h264`: **84 passed**, 4 ignored (includes existing `inter.rs` tests and cheap conformance).
- New test: random 8-bit rows, widths 4/8/16 plus odd 5/9/15/17, SIMD vs `htap_row_scalar` / `vtap_row_scalar`.
- Optional `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-h264 --test perf -- --ignored` **did run** (fixture already local):
  - 1080p High CRF20, 120 frames: **1 thread 110.8 fps** (1.083s); **12 threads 592.7 fps** (0.202s).
  - This is a whole-decoder number, not a kernel microbench; treat as a baseline after the spike, not a claimed 3× close.

## Remaining work (not this PR)

- Other hot kernels (IDCT / inverse quant, chroma bilinear, deblock, weighted pred).
- Pipelined entropy vs residual.
- Only if safe SIMD is not enough: an **ADR** for hand-written `unsafe` intrinsics (explicitly out of scope here).
- Packaging `target-cpu` (not `nati…

title: h264: safe-SIMD weighted pred, chroma, and IDCT add (#848)
author: vbasky
body:
# #848 throughput — remaining safe-SIMD kernels (after 6-tap / PR #883)

This is more of **storytold/filmcraft#848’s throughput half**: additional H.264 decoder kernels after the 6-tap luma spike (`feat/848-h264-safe-simd`, PR #883). It is **not** LongGOP seek (#876). **No `unsafe`**, no ADR, no `-C target-cpu=native`. Pipelined entropy remains a later PR.

Stacked on #883 (6-tap luma). Merge that first, or take both commits here.

## Files

- `crates/h264/src/inter.rs`
- `crates/h264/src/transform.rs`

## Kernels SIMD’d vs skipped

| Kernel | Status |
| --- | --- |
| **weighted_store** (default avg + weighted, uni/bi) | **SIMD** `wide::i32x8` body for widths 8/16; scalar tail |
| **Chroma bilinear** (`mc_chroma_win`) | **SIMD** `i32x8` for the 4-tap eighth-sample mix; scalar tail; integer copy path unchanged |
| **IDCT reconstruction** (`idct4_add` / `idct8_add` add+clip) | **SIMD** `i32x4` / `i32x8` clip-add |
| **idct8_1d** | **SIMD** eight columns at once as `i32x8` lanes (`idct8_1d_lanes`); row 1D stays scalar butterfly (cross-lane); bit-exact vs scalar 1D |
| **Deblock `filter_lanes`** | **Skipped.** Already branch-free per-lane so LLVM vectorises; rewriting in `wide` would risk 8.7.2 behaviour for little gain |

## Tests

- Existing H.264 transform reference tests kept (`vectorised_transforms_match_reference`, DC/hand examples).
- New: `chroma_simd_matches_scalar`, `weighted_store_simd_matches_scalar` (random widths including 4/5/8/9/16), `idct8_1d_lanes_match_scalar`.
- `rtk cargo test -p filmcraft-h264`: **87 passed, 4 ignored** (ignored are fixture/perf tests).

## Perf

Not run. Optional ignored perf needs local fixtures; skipped.

## Risk

Low–medium: bit-exact arithmetic vs scalar on random data, but reconstruction clip uses `min`/`max` instead of `clamp`. Weighted paths still wrap like scalar `i32` muls. Chroma/weight SIMD only kicks in at width ≥ 8 (4×4 chroma/blocks stay scalar). No ABI/ADR change.

title: monitors: show the unreadable slate for persistently failing (damaged) media
author: FredApps
body:
Follow-up to #762 for the case it leaves out on purpose, as invited in #768. Part of #626.

## Problem
#762 maps only `Unsupported` decoder errors to the MEDIA UNREADABLE slate. As @echelon explained on #768, `Decode`/`Io` errors are left alone because transient ones (the web build's "still decoding" frames, a one-off I/O hiccup) must not flash a slate or end up in exports. But a genuinely damaged file, where every frame fails, still renders silent black with no explanation.

## Fix
- `crates/engine/src/media_pool.rs`: `MediaPool::monitor_source(item, src)` wraps a source in a private `DamagedAsSlate`. It counts `Decode`/`Io` failures per item; after `DAMAGED_AFTER = 3` in a row, failing frames return the existing Unreadable `SlateSource` frame. Any successful frame resets the count, so the slate clears as soon as decoding recovers.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`: the frame server's `JobProvider` (Source/Program monitors, thumbnails) uses `monitor_source`. This is the only caller.

Why 3: one bad slice or read hiccup (plus a retry of it) stays as today; three consecutive failures are about 1/8 s at 24 fps, so a damaged file is flagged almost immediately.

How echelon's concerns are excluded:
- **Still decoding / still loading (web):** those reads call `filmcraft_media::pending::mark()`. A failure while the pending flag is set neither counts nor resets the run, and the flag is left for the frame server to `take()` as before.
- **Exports / offline render / frame export:** they read the pool's sources (`full_res_provider`, `PoolProvider`) directly and never go through `monitor_source`, so the slate can't be burned in. Nothing is written to the item's offline status either.
- `Cancelled`, `NoStream` and `Unsupported` (already handled by #762) pass through unchanged. Audio is untouched.

No renderer, decoder, dependency or contributor changes.

## Tests (`media_pool::tests`)
- `monitors_show_the_slate_for_persistently_failing_frames_only`: Decode and Io failures below …

title: #847: AV1 decode runs deblocking, CDEF and loop restoration in parallel row bands
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G16 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #847.

## Problem

The AV1 decoder ran deblocking, CDEF and loop restoration on one thread per frame (`postfilter::apply` took the pool as `_pool` and never used it). A single-tile stream, which SVT-AV1 and most encoders write by default, has no other parallelism inside a frame. References are waited for as whole frames, so this serial tail (a quarter to a third of a frame) sat on the critical path of every frame that references it.

## Fix

- The three filters run in bands of 64 luma rows on the decoder's existing rayon pool, with one join per filter per frame. No new dependency. With one thread (wasm32, `threads` feature off, `Decoder::with_threads(1)`) everything runs as one band, so the code path is the old one.
- **CDEF and loop restoration**: every block or unit reads only the input frames and writes only its own rows of a separate output. Each band gets disjoint row slices of all three planes (`Plane::row_bands` / `FrameBuf::row_bands`, safe `split_at_mut`).
- **Loop filter**: vertical edges touch only their own 4 rows. A horizontal edge reads at most `filter_size / 2` samples on each side, never more than the transform blocks on either side are high. So no two edges touch the same sample, and any order gives the spec's raster-order result. Transform blocks never cross a 64-row boundary, so only a band's top edges reach into the band above. Each band refilters the vertical edges of an unfiltered copy of the 8 rows above it (the same values the band above computes), runs its top edges against that copy, and writes back only the samples they changed. The band above never touches those samples. This replaced a first version that split the work into one join per plane and pass, 9 joins per frame. On this busy machine each join costs a worker wake-up, and that version made deblocking slower.
- `tests/perf.rs` adds a low-delay 1080p fixture (each frame references the previous one), a single-tile 2160p GOP, the all-core per-stage br…

title: #243: text fields keep unmodified keys so IMEs can compose
author: opentechnepal
body:
Part of the typing half of #243. The Delete-key half was fixed by #261.

## Problem

Vietnamese cannot be typed into any text field. Vietnamese Telex composes diacritics from **plain unmodified letters**:

| Telex | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `a` + `s` | á |
| `a` + `r` | ả |
| `a` + `j` | ạ |
| `z` | remove diacritic |

The editor binds unmodified single-key shortcuts for its tools and playback:

`A` Track Select Forward · `B` Ripple Edit · `C` Razor · `H` Hand · `J` Shuttle Left · `K` Shuttle Stop · `L` Shuttle Right · `N` Rolling Edit · `P` Pen · `R` Rate Stretch · `T` Type · `U` Slide · `V` Selection · `Y` Slip · `Z` Zoom

`handle_shortcuts` calls `consume_key` for every binding before any widget reads the pass, so it swallowed those presses and the IME never saw them. **No diacritic could be typed**, and plain `a`/`c`/`t` were stolen as well. This also matches the Korean IME symptom in storytold/artcraft#2093.

## Fix

A focused text field now owns unmodified keys.

`egui_wants_keyboard_input` was already checked, but it is the wrong guard twice over:

1. it is read **before** the pass lays the UI out, so it still reports the previous pass;
2. it is true for **any** focused widget, so relying on it would leave the editor without its single-key tool shortcuts while a slider or a panel has focus.

`text_edit_focused` is the precise check, so the guard is narrow:

```rust
fn lets_text_field_keep(modifiers: egui::Modifiers, text_focused: bool) -> bool {
    text_focused && menus::specificity(modifiers) == 0
}
```

Chords with a modifier still fire while a field is focused: an IME does not consume Ctrl+S and friends. Esc for trim cancel is handled before the guard and is unaffected. `Space` (Play/Stop) keeps working whenever no field is focused.

## Tests

`text_focus_shortcut_tests` covers the four cases: the plain keys reach a focused field, the tool shortcuts still fire without one, a modified chord fires either way, and the Telex trigger keys (`s f r x j w z`…

title: fix(macos): declare microphone permission for voice-over recording (close #659)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

FilmCraft v0.5.0 on Apple Silicon macOS can never open the microphone: neither the built-in Mac mic nor an external one works for voice-over. Two things have to be in place for macOS to grant audio-input:

- `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` in `Info.plist` (the user-visible prompt).
- `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` in the signed entitlements.

Both were missing, so the app never appears under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone** and the user can't grant the permission.

`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`: add `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` with a one-sentence explanation.

`packaging/macos/entitlements.plist`: add the `audio-input` device entitlement. The comment that said *"Deliberately empty"* is updated to *"Deliberately minimal"* — voice-over is the first real exception, with a one-line reason in the comment.

`plutil -lint` on both files ✓. No source-code change — runtime code in `filmcraft::audio::*` doesn't need any work.

Closes #659.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
A page that frames FilmCraft on the same origin can now open clips and projects in it and store what it saves, through postMessage, instead of saved projects and exports becoming browser downloads. Built for a Nextcloud integration, but nothing in it is host-specific.

Only the web shell changes (src/host.rs):
- filmcraft:open { name, path, blob } from the parent: a project (.fcproj) opens; any other file is imported into a new project named after it. Files keep the parent's path in the virtual file table, under /host, so projects refer to them by it.
- Before a project opens, media it refers to under /host that aren't here yet are asked of the parent (filmcraft:need { paths }) and arrive as filmcraft:file { path, blob }; one that can't be had stays offline for File > Link Media.
- Written files (saved projects, exports) go to the parent (filmcraft:save): a file under /host by the parent's path, anything else by its file name, for the parent to ask where it goes.
- filmcraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; filmcraft:ready and filmcraft:failed report start-up. In host mode the demo project and the recovery snapshot don't open.
- fs::put_blob registers a Blob at a given path; import::import_registered imports a file already in the table.

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: #402: animated GIF and APNG import as clips, with transparency
author: liangforstudy
body:
Fixes #402 , follow up of #597 

APNG and animated GIF files opened as stills showing only their first frame. They now open as movie clips (crates/media/src/animated.rs):

- every frame is decoded and composited onto the full canvas by the image crate (APNG blend/dispose ops, GIF disposal), keeping alpha
- each frame lasts its own delay; GIF delays <= 10 ms play as 100 ms and APNG delays < 10 ms as 10 ms, as browsers do

- hostile input: at most 10,000 frames / 1 GiB of decoded pictures; a damaged frame ends the clip at the frames before it; files with one frame (or none that decode) still open as stills, as before

Tests: media unit tests (timing, transparency, merging, single-frame files stay stills, truncated/bit-flipped files never panic) and an engine test that imports an animated GIF and reopens it from a saved project.

title: fix(timeline): create a sequence when dropping a file on an empty timeline
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Dragging a media file from the operating system's file explorer onto an empty Timeline imports the file into the Project panel but does not create a sequence or place the media.

The empty Timeline indicates that users can drop media there to create a sequence.

Addresses #785

title: fix(media): RF64 trailing metadata stays outside audio duration
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #925

## Summary

RF64 WAV files with metadata chunks after the audio data were incorrectly reporting extended duration and returning metadata bytes as decoded audio samples. A 4-frame file with a trailing iXML chunk became 17 frames, with the extra 13 frames being the iXML chunk interpreted as PCM.

## Changes

- `crates/media/src/wav.rs`: Parse the RF64 `ds64` chunk and use its `dataSize` when the `data` chunk size is the RF64 sentinel (`0xFFFFFFFF`), instead of reading to EOF
- `crates/codecs/tests/rf64_metadata.rs`: New integration test covering RF64 with trailing metadata and both control cases (RF64 without trailing chunk, RIFF with trailing chunk)

## Restoration criteria met

- RF64 file with trailing iXML chunk reports 21168000 ticks (4 frames at 48kHz) instead of 89964000 (17 frames)
- Reading 20 samples returns 20 zeros, not 4 zeros + 13 samples of metadata + 3 zeros
- Both control cases still return 4 frames and silence
- All 4 existing WAV unit tests pass

## Edge cases handled

- Missing `ds64` chunk: falls back to rest-of-file (old behavior, no regression)
- `ds64.dataSize` larger than file: capped to actual file length
- `ds64.dataSize` zero or too small: follows EBU 3306 spec (optional hardening: treat zero as unknown)

## Bonus fix

Trailing `iXML`/`bext` chunks in RF64 files are now parsed for time reference instead of being consumed as audio.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs` passes
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean
- Focused `rf64_metadata` test catches the bug when old code is restored

— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: Import FCPXML one-frame markers as points
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #909.

FCPXML encodes a point marker as one frame at the sequence rate. Import compared that duration to 1 tick, so a 24 fps point became a one-frame range (and FilmCraft points round-tripped the same way).

A marker whose duration is at most one sequence frame now imports as a FilmCraft point (`duration = 0`). Real ranges of two or more frames are unchanged.

title: Export FCP7 XML markers on source media
author: vbasky
body:

title: Export: correct loudness lost to peak limiting
author: earlvanze
body:
Loudness normalization measures the mix before applying its peak limiter, so a requested integrated loudness can be missed when limiting reduces the final signal. Re-measure the limited output and apply a bounded gain correction before limiting, then reset the audio cursor and limiter for delivery.

The search uses at most four limited-output trials, at most 3 dB additional gain per step and 9 dB total additional drive. It retains the best trial and stops within 0.1 LU or when improvement plateaus. Infeasible loudness targets retain the peak ceiling. Cancellation remains checked between chunks.

Synthetic regression coverage includes a quiet bed with large peaks, an infeasible target, cancellation during correction, and unchanged output length/alignment. No dependency on the GPU, audio DSP, layout, or export-watchdog PRs.

Isolated branch validation: all 97 export library tests passed, export all-target Clippy passed with `-D warnings`, and formatting/diff checks passed. Full workspace validation completed on exact commit `5d7dc800a86375e642edd3580d078367e1730cab`. Formatting, release workspace all-target Clippy with `-D warnings`, dependency layers, asset attribution, and WASM checks (44 crates) passed. A complete `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast` sweep recorded **2,843 passed, one failed, and 41 ignored**, including doctests. The sole failure was the existing render throughput assertion described below. In the combined recovery build, the high-crest fixture changed from −17.151 LUFS to −14.056 LUFS at a −14 target while retaining a −2.000 dBTP ceiling. A complete 12,474-frame 4K Mac export measured −14.07 LUFS after AAC encoding. That end-to-end result is from the combined recovery build, not this isolated branch. Encoded AAC peak was −1.34 dBTP; this change does not claim that lossy encoding preserves the PCM peak ceiling.
